scope_allowed: Relevance of the validation activities to the COU

models.name: Model A: Explicit-thread Screw in Cortico-cancellous Vertebral Segment
models.what_it_computes: Nonlinear force–displacement response during axial extraction, thread flank contact pressure distribution, local bone plastic strain and damage indices, and predicted initiation of pullout.

models.name: Model B: Axisymmetric Unit-Cell Interface with Anisotropic Bone Surrogate
models.what_it_computes: Effective interface shear capacity, initial purchase stiffness (pre-yield slope), insertion-torque proxy from frictional seating work, and progressive loss of engagement under small-amplitude cyclic loading.

mechanisms.name: Monotonic axial pullout
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Determines the maximum resistance to extraction during adverse loading and provides a benchmark for primary fixation strength.

mechanisms.name: Immediate post-insertion purchase
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Captures primary stability at time zero, informing likelihood of micromotion before fusion and correlation with insertion torque.

mechanisms.name: Low-amplitude cyclic toggling
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Assesses early loosening pathways from physiologic micromotion that degrade thread engagement without catastrophic failure.

mechanisms.name: Transverse pedicle wall strip-out
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Evaluates off-axis load transfer and risk of pedicle wall compromise that can precipitate loss of fixation.

deviation.detail: All credibility factors are scored on a 0–12 confidence index (0, 4, 8, 12) with rationales recorded per model-by-mechanism cell.

expected_decision.outcome_source: The analysis supports use of Model A for evaluating axial pullout and immediate engagement within the specified use range and qualified use of Model B for insertion-related metrics and small-amplitude cyclic degradation.

models: Model A, a three-dimensional representation of an explicit-thread titanium screw embedded in a cortico-cancellous vertebral segment
Model B, an axisymmetric unit-cell interface model representing thread–bone engagement with an anisotropic surrogate for trabecular microstructure
datasets: cadaveric thoracolumbar vertebrae (n = 18 for pullout, n = 14 for insertion torque, n = 10 for toggling, n = 6 for transverse loading), quasi-static pullout per ASTM F543 (5 mm/min, 37 °C Ringer’s), instrumented insertion torque, cyclic lateral displacement at ±0.3 mm and 2 Hz with a 150 N compressive bias, and lateral strip-out to failure
cortical–cancellous coupon tests, yielding a coefficient of 0.24 (SD 0.05, n = 12 donors)
foam-block corroboration used only for independent verification of the driver system (n = 8 blocks, 15 pcf nominal density)
acceptance_criteria: within the predefined 10% tolerance for central tendency

spans: In both models, frictional work dominated the seating resistance, with less than 10% contribution from elastic indentation at peaks, supporting the use of frictional work as a torque surrogate in this device.

spans: The seating-work torque proxy in both models was computed by integrating tangential traction times circumferential sliding distance over the engaged interface and dividing by the instantaneous rotation rate; this proxy was compared to measured insertion torque to assess whether sliding friction dominated seating resistance.

spans: For immediate engagement, Model A’s computation of frictional seating work integrated over the engaged interface produced a torque proxy of 1.05 N·m against the instrumented 6 edicle screw FEA driver’s 1.10 N·m mean, a 5% difference.
The pre-yield axial stiffness immediately after seating was predicted as 2.9 kN/mm compared with 3.0 kN/mm measured.
